note: Rules for the world sketch: the large undersea features that islands grow from. Distances in meters unless the name says tiles. Rerun tools/build_sketch.gd after editing.

shelves.note: One continental shelf around each pair of inner and outer starters. Islands on it come from rolling hills breaking the surface.

starter_islands.note: Poleward shores are rocky and steep, equator-facing shores have long sandy beaches with a flat coastal plain for the town and a sheltered bay for the port.
starter_islands.strait_note: A strait this wide (meters past the coast) keeps shelf hills from joining the starter island, so the starter landmass stays in its size range (landmass_km2, checked by a test). Smaller neighbors may still join by a narrow land bridge.

trench_arc.note: A curved chain of volcanoes along one side of the central trench, bowed toward it like real arcs.

ridge.note: A mid-ocean ridge winding along the dangerous east-west edge and across both poles.

danger_effects.note: How danger shapes land: steeper peaks, cliffs and narrow shelves where it is dangerous, gentle shores near starters.
